claims.text: The highest offset this candidate may keep after ``n_same`` attempts.
claims.why: The function returns a float, but the concept of 'highest offset' and 'keep' is not defined in this chunk; BAND_SPAN is undefined.

claims.text: Repeats COMPOUND. One worktree failure is an accident; five in a row is a broken task, and a policy that treated them alike would leave the loop re-picking a candidate it cannot even check out -- the original defect, reintroduced through the outcomes that were judged harmless. ``residual ** n`` is monotone, bounded, and never actually reaches the floor while ``residual > 0``, so a compounding sink is still a penalty and still never a filter.
claims.why: The docstring explains the rationale but makes no testable claim about this code's behaviour that can be verified from the chunk alone.

claims.text: Never raises and never returns ``None``: the caller is on the ranking path, where a missing row must degrade to the safest reading rather than to a traceback or -- far worse -- to no penalty at all.
claims.why: The function always returns OutcomePolicy (either from OUTCOME_POLICY or UNKNOWN_OUTCOME), never None, and no raise is present.

claims.text: The DEFINITION half of a candidate's retry identity.
claims.why: The concept of 'retry identity' and 'definition half' is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``task_id`` is lineage, not definition: an inventory id hashes ``area|name|status`` only, so the tests, entrypoints, notes and therefore the whole generated INSTRUCTION can change while the id stays byte-identical. Joining memory on the id alone would make a rewritten task inherit the old one's failures and sink on evidence about work nobody is proposing any more.
claims.why: References task_id, inventory id, and memory which are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Deliberately excludes score and evidence: those move on every inventory edit and are not what makes two attempts the same attempt.
claims.why: The function only takes instruction as argument and hashes it; no score or evidence inputs are used.

claims.text: A drift test pins OUTCOME_POLICY's keys against attempt.ATTEMPT_STATES, so a newly added state is a RED test rather than a silent fall through to here.
claims.why: References attempt.ATTEMPT_STATES and a drift test not present in this chunk.
